newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: DBS Land expects Hong Kong profit in '97.
newsitem.headline: DBS Land expects Hong Kong profit in '97.

text.p: DBS Land plans to launch three residential projects comprising 824 units in Hong Kong in 1997, group chief operating officer Han Cheng Fong said an interview published in the DBS Land 1996 annual report.

"Maiden earnings from Hong Kong will flow in this year and strong growth is expected in the next few years as we progressively launch our seven projects," he said in the report made available on Tuesday.
"Given current market conditions, profit margins of these projects are expected to be good."
Han said recent government measures to cool speculation in Hong Kong's property market would not lead to a downturn in prices as "the strong underlying housing demand far exceeds potential supply".
He said the group's regionalisation effort had paid off with overseas earnings rising to 13 percent of pre-tax profit in 1996 from just two percent in 1994.

The property group, which chalked up a 31 percent rise in 1996 net profit to Singapore $207.3 million, was on track to generate 30 to 40 percent of its earnings from overseas by the year 2000, he said.
DBS Land is also confident of the property market in Shanghai despite the current oversupply in commercial properties.

Han said he expected "the down cycle to be short because of Shanghai's strong economic growth which averaged 13 percent per annum in the past several years and which is likely to be sustained in the medium term".

He was also optimistic about earnings from Singapore. "Profit recognition of residential units sold will underpin trading income over the next two years. The launch of another six residential projects in Singapore in 1997 and 1998 will
He also said the planned listing of the group's hotel interest held under Raffles Holdings was scheduled for 1997 subject to approval from the authorities and also market conditions.
